test.title: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry - Test 3
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: The number of chlorine atoms in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of chlorine gas at STP is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>21</mn></msup></math>. (Round off to the Nearest Integer). [Assume chlorine is an ideal gas at STP <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>083</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mo> </mo><mi>bar</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>023</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>23</mn></msup><mo>]</mo></math>

A solution of sugar is obtained by mixing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of its <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></math> solution and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo></math>of its <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo>%</mo><mo> </mo></math>solution (both by mass). The mass percentage of the resulting sugar solution is _______ (Nearest integer)

Consider the following reaction occurring in the blast furnace:
$\mathrm{Fe}_3 \mathrm{O}_{4(\mathrm{~s})}+4 \mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow 3 \mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{l})}+4 \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}$
' $x$ ' kg of iron is produced when $2.32 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{Fe}_3 \mathrm{O}_4$ and $2.8 \times 10^2 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{CO}$ are brought together in the furnace. The value of ' $x$ ' is _____. (nearest integer)
Given:
molar mass of $\mathrm{Fe}_3 \mathrm{O}_4=232 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
molar mass of $\mathrm{CO}=28 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
molar mass of $\left.\mathrm{Fe}=56 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right\}$

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>56</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> of nitrogen gas is mixed with excess of hydrogen gas and it is found that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> of ammonia gas is produced, The volume of unused nitrogen gas is found to be_____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math>.

9.3 g of aniline is subjected to reaction with excess of acetic anhydride to prepare acetanilide. The mass of acetanilide produced if the reaction is 100% completed is _____×10-1 g.

(Given molar mass in g mol-1 N=14,O=16,C=12,H=1)
$6.023 \times 10^{22}$ molecules are present in 10 g of a substance ' $x$ '. The molarity of a solution containing 5 g of substance ' $x$ ' in 2 L solution is $\_\_\_\_$ $\times 10^{-3}$

When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mi>mol</mi></math> of an organic compound containing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>%</mo></math> carbon was burnt completely, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> was produced. The molar mass of compound is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>gmol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> (Nearest integer)

The number of atoms in 8 g of sodium is x×1023. The value of x is _____ . (Nearest integer)

 Given : NA=6.02×1023 mol-1 Atomic mass of Na=23.0u]

Molarity \((\mathrm{M})\) of an aqueous solution containing \(x \mathrm{~g}\) of anhyd. \(\mathrm{CuSO}_4\) in \(500 \mathrm{~mL}\) solution at \(32{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\) is \(2 \times 10^{-1} \mathrm{M}\). Its molality will be ______ \(\times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}\). (nearest integer). [Given density of the solution \(=1.25 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mL}\)]

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> aqueous solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>02</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi><mo> </mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>.</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of this solution is diluted with deionized water to give <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> solution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mfenced></math>. In solution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mfenced></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> are added. Total <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> mols of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> in the final solution is____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi>moles</mi></math>.

A 100 mL solution was made by adding 1.43 g of Na2CO3.xH2O. The normality of the solution is 0.1 N. The value of x is _______

(The atomic mass of Na is 23g/mol)

0.1 mol of the following given antiviral compound
\((\mathrm{P})\) will weigh ________ \(\times 10^{-1} \mathrm{~g}\)

(Given : molar mass in \(\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1} \mathrm{H}: 1, \mathrm{C}: 12, \mathrm{~N}: 14\), \(\mathrm{O}: 16, \mathrm{~F}: 19, \mathrm{I}: 127)\)

Quantitative analysis of an organic compound (X) shows following % composition.

C : $14.5 \%$
Cl : 64.46%
H: 1.8 %
(Empirical formula mass of the compound $(\mathrm{X})$ is __________ $\times 10^{-1}$
(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{C}: 12, \mathrm{H}: 1, \mathrm{O}: 16, \mathrm{Cl}: 35.5$)

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of propane is completely reacted with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of oxygen. The mole fraction of carbon dioxide in the resulting mixture is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is (Nearest integer)

In the given reaction,

X+Y+3Z⇄XYZ3

if one mole of each of X and Y with 0.05 mol of Z gives compound XYZ3. (Given : Atomic masses of X,Y and Z are 10,20 and 30amu, respectively). The yield of XYZ3 is____g.

0.01 mole of an organic compound $(X)$ containing $10 \%$ hydrogen, on complete combustion produced $0.9 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$. Molar mass of $(\mathrm{X})$ is _____ $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.

<math><mn>10.30</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is dissolved into a liter of sea water of density <math><mn>1.03</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> . The concentration of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> in ppm is _____________.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> mole of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>PbS</mi></math> is oxidised by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> moles of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> to get <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></math> moles of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>.</mo></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mo>=</mo></math>

On complete combustion, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>492</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of an organic compound gave <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>792</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math> of carbon in the organic compound is (Nearest integer)

The volume strength of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><msub><mi>MH</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> solution calculated at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>273</mn><mo> </mo><mi>K</mi></math> and 1 atm is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>........</mo><mfenced><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.0821</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mo> </mo><mi>atm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math> (rounded off to the nearest integer)
